title: Stop the Scroll in 3 Seconds

sections.heading: Everyday Analogy - The Shop Window
sections.body:
Imagine people scrolling like walking past shop windows without stopping.

A hook is the first line of your post or video. Its job is to stop someone in 3 seconds. A storytelling template is a ready-made sentence with blanks, like Mad Libs, that you fill with your own story.

For example: "I didn't plan to talk about this, but pretending (insert situation) was fine wasn't working anymore." You just insert your situation and it becomes yours.

sections.heading: Why It Exists
sections.body:
On Instagram and short-form video, attention is short. If you don't grab it instantly, people keep scrolling.

These 50 hooks exist to solve that. Audience engagement means likes, comments, shares, and watch time. Fill-in-the-blank copywriting gives you proven, attention-grabbing starters so you don't stare at a blank page. You keep your message, but start stronger.

sections.heading: What Can Go Wrong
sections.body:
A hook promises a story. If the rest of your content doesn't deliver, people feel tricked and leave.

Problems happen when:
- You copy the template word-for-word without adding your real details
- You use a dramatic hook for a boring tip
- You use the same 2-3 hooks every post, so followers get bored

The fix is simple: match the hook to a true story you actually tell.

steps.narration: People scroll fast past hundreds of posts.
Your first line is a fill-in-the-blank hook to grab attention in 3 seconds.
A good hook makes them pause instead of scrolling.
You must then tell the real story you promised.
If the story matches, they like, comment, and share.

quiz.q: What is a hook in this context?
options: The last line that asks for a follow
The first 3-second line that stops scrolling
A hashtag that hides your post
quiz.why: Your save defines hooks as attention-grabbers designed to stop scrolling in 3 seconds.

quiz.q: What fails first if you use the same viral hook on every post without a matching story?
options: People feel tricked, get bored, and stop engaging
quiz.why: A hook only works if the story delivers; repeat or mismatched hooks break trust and engagement drops.

options: An app that posts for you
quiz.why: The save gives 50 fill-in-the-blank templates like 'I didn't plan to talk about this, but...' where you insert your situation.

extra: Test hooks by reading only the first line aloud - if a stranger wouldn't pause, rewrite it.
